sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式真的很不一样。

sentences.zh: 我以前非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开Whoop应用，看我的睡眠、压力、运动强度是如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及日常状态相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝对算不上什么精英运动员，但我确实受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢了解更多关于自己身体的知识。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day-to-day
sentences.zh: Whoop还给我提供这些切实可行的个性化见解，让我做事更有意识，这意味着我在日常生活中能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.zh: 去关注我真正需要什么，而不是一味地踩油门、拼命往前冲。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20岁心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨20岁时的一些重大生活变化和转变，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Today is International Women's Day and I thought, what better way to celebrate than to bring my mum on the show to discuss motherhood, feminism, being a leader,
sentences.zh: 今天是国际妇女节，我想，还有什么比邀请我妈妈上节目更好的庆祝方式呢，我们来聊聊母职、女性主义、如何成为一名领导者、

sentences.en: a successful woman in a male-dominated industry, all of the above.
sentences.zh: 在男性主导的行业中做一名成功的女性，等等诸如此类的话题。

sentences.en: She is a pretty cool lady and my personal hero.
sentences.zh: 她是一个相当酷的女性，也是我的个人偶像。

sentences.en: I know that sounds cliche, but I am super lucky to have had such a wonderful role model who has a lot of wisdom to share and I thought you guys could benefit
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来像是个老生常谈，但我真的超级幸运，能有这样一个拥有许多人生智慧、堪称完美榜样的母亲，我想你们也能从她的智慧中受益。

sentences.en: from some of that wisdom as well.
sentences.zh: 其中一些智慧。

sentences.en: This episode is part of iHeart's International Women's Day initiative called Women Take the Mic.
sentences.zh: 本期节目是iHeart国际妇女节“女性发声”（Women Take the Mic）企划的一部分。

sentences.en: You can find a bunch of other interviews just like this one by searching Women Take the Mic wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在任何收听播客的地方搜索“Women Take the Mic”，找到一大批像这样的精彩采访。

sentences.en: Let's jump into the interview.
sentences.zh: 让我们直接进入采访吧。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身在世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，和我们一起剖析20岁时的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to be doing something a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要搞点不一样的。

sentences.en: I know I say that every guest is my favourite, but honestly, this one I think kind of has to take the cake by obligation because they are blood.
sentences.zh: 我知道我每次都说某个嘉宾是我的最老朋友，但说实话，这一期我觉得非她莫属，因为我们有血缘关系。

sentences.en: I thought it's International Women's Day today.
sentences.zh: 我想今天是国际妇女节嘛。

sentences.en: Who better to talk to?
sentences.zh: 还有谁比这更适合聊天呢？

sentences.en: Who is more my hero than my own mother?
sentences.zh: 谁能比我自己的母亲更能称得上是我的偶像呢？

sentences.en: So today I'm bringing on my mum to come and have a chat with me.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我请我妈妈来跟我聊聊天。

sentences.en: So we talk about mother-daughter dynamics, motherhood, being a successful woman in business as she is, and feminism and all the good things that come with it.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了母女关系、母亲身份、像她一样在商界成为一个成功的女性，还有女性主义以及与之相关的所有美好事物。

sentences.en: So, hey, mum.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗨，妈妈。

sentences.en: How are you going?
sentences.zh: 近来怎么样？

sentences.en: Hey, Gem.
sentences.zh: 嗨，杰姆（Gem）。

sentences.en: You were saying to me that you were nervous before this.
sentences.zh: 你刚才跟我说你录之前挺紧张的。

sentences.en: I'm a bit nervous.
sentences.zh: 我是有点紧张。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Oh, because I probably haven't been, well, I haven't been interviewed by you before.
sentences.zh: 哦，因为我可能没被……嗯，我以前没被你采访过。

sentences.en: And it's a different dynamic.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种不同的动态关系。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, I want to do well by you.
sentences.zh: 当然了，你知道的，我想在你面前表现好一点。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: You want to impress the listeners?
sentences.zh: 你想给听众留下好印象？

sentences.en: Well, I just, I don't want to let you down.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是，我不想让你失望。

sentences.en: I don't want to come across as not being worthy of your wonderful pod.
sentences.zh: 我不想显得配不上你这个精彩的播客。

sentences.en: Oh, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 噢，没关系。

sentences.en: I will defend you to the death.
sentences.zh: 我会誓死捍卫你的。

sentences.en: If anyone says anything, I'll be like,
sentences.zh: 如果有人说什么，我就会说：

sentences.en: that's my mother you're talking about.
sentences.zh: “你在说我妈呢。”

sentences.en: So, block deleted.
sentences.zh: 然后，直接拉黑删除。

sentences.en: I honestly think this will be a great chat because we have a good relationship, both as a mother and daughter and as kind of friends as well.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我觉得这会是一次非常棒的聊天，因为我们不仅是母女，关系很好，而且也有点像朋友。

sentences.en: Yeah, me too.
sentences.zh: 对，我也是这么觉得。

sentences.en: I'm looking, I'm looking forward to it.
sentences.zh: 我很期待，我挺期待的。

sentences.en: It's just, it's a different dynamic for me.
sentences.zh: 只是，对我来说这是一种不同的相处模式。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm in charge.
sentences.zh: 对，我说了算。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're in my turf.
sentences.zh: 对，在你的地盘上。

sentences.en: I can't hang up.
sentences.zh: 我都不能挂电话。

sentences.en: You can't hang up.
sentences.zh: 你不能挂电话。

sentences.en: We're blood related.
sentences.zh: 我们有血缘关系。

sentences.en: So, I wanted to bring you on because obviously it's International Women's Day.
sentences.zh: 所以我想把你请来，很明显是因为今天是国际妇女节。

sentences.en: And I was thinking, let's do a special episode for this.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我们要不就为此做一期特别节目吧。

sentences.en: Let's do an episode talking about what it means to be a woman, to identify as a woman.
sentences.zh: 我们就做一期节目，聊聊身为女性、认同自己为女性意味着什么。

sentences.en: And part of what comes with that is also like a discussion around like our relationship with our mothers and a relationship with our parents and all these other things,
sentences.zh: 其中一部分也顺便讨论一下我们与母亲的关系、与父母的关系以及所有这些其他事情，

sentences.en: how like our childhood informs the women that we grow up to be.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的童年是如何塑造了我们长大后成为的女性。

sentences.en: And I thought that we could do a little deep dive into what it was like for you to become my mum because I'm the eldest daughter.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以深入探讨一下你成为我母亲的经历是什么样的，因为我是长女嘛。

sentences.en: You're also the eldest daughter.
sentences.zh: 你也是长女。

sentences.en: And just like what I was like as a child, what it was like becoming a mother, like I said, and then what it's like to run a business basically, which you do.
sentences.zh: 还有我小时候是什么样的，成为母亲是什么样的，就像我说的，然后经营一家公司又是什么样的，基本上你就是这么做的。

sentences.en: Well, you're a CEO.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你是个首席执行官（CEO）。

sentences.en: So what that's like.
sentences.zh: 所以那种感觉是怎样的。

sentences.en: Well, certainly plenty to talk about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那确实有很多话题可以聊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm going to start with the hard-hitting questions.
sentences.zh: 我要从那些犀利的问题开始。

sentences.en: Okay, go for it.
sentences.zh: 行，尽管问吧。

sentences.en: Because I wanted to know this as well.
sentences.zh: 因为我也想知道这个。

sentences.en: What was I like as a child?
sentences.zh: 我小时候是什么样的？

sentences.en: Do you remember?
sentences.zh: 你还记得吗？

sentences.en: I'd be embarrassed if you don't.
sentences.zh: 如果你不记得的话我会觉得很尴尬的。

sentences.en: No, the funny thing is you really do remember.
sentences.zh: 不，有趣的是你真的记得。

sentences.en: And I suspect that there's, I need to be a bit careful because of course memories change over time and you think you remember certain things.
sentences.zh: 而且我猜，我得稍微小心点，因为记忆当然会随着时间而改变，你会觉得你记得某些事情。

sentences.en: I'm sure you remember some things differently to the way I remember them.
sentences.zh: 我确信你对某些事情的记忆和我的记忆是不一样的。

sentences.en: We can get to that.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿可以聊到这个。

sentences.en: But actually the really interesting thing is when I sort of think back on you and your sisters,
sentences.zh: 但实际上非常有趣的一点是，当我回想起你和你的姐妹们时，

sentences.en: I've got really clear memories of the days each of you were born, my sort of very clear first impressions of each of you.
sentences.zh: 我对你们每个人的出生日期都有着非常清晰的记忆，对你们每个人的第一印象也非常清晰。

sentences.en: And it's funny, you're all different.
sentences.zh: 说来有趣，你们各不相同。

sentences.en: I remember, so what I remember of you the day you were born, and by the way, you had to come in, you know, with a bang.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我记得你出生那天的样子，顺便说一句，你出场时还真是“轰轰烈烈”。

sentences.en: You were an emergency Caesar child.
sentences.zh: 你是剖腹产紧急生下来的。

sentences.en: So there was that.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: There was that.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: But the thing I remember was in amongst all of this sort of calm chaos was you sort of coming out with these big eyes
sentences.zh: 但我记得的事情是，在所有这种平静的混乱之中，你睁着一双大眼睛出来了，

sentences.en: just sort of slowly blinking at the world as if to say, you know, where am I?
sentences.zh: 只是在这个世界上缓缓地眨着眼睛，仿佛在说：

sentences.en: What have I come to?
sentences.zh: “这是哪儿？我来到了一个什么地方？”

sentences.en: But not crying so much and just sort of, you know, trying to sort of focus straight out of the gate, trying to focus on what was around you
sentences.zh: 但你没有怎么哭闹，只是，你知道的，一出来就试图集中注意力，试图看清周围的事物，

sentences.en: and trying to make sense of it is what it felt like.
sentences.zh: 并且试图去理解它，当时给人的感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: I can't remember that, but.
sentences.zh: 我不记得那个了，不过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you were quiet as a little baby for the first week or so, but that changed.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，作为一个小婴儿，你在第一个星期左右非常安静，但后来情况就变了。

sentences.en: But the other thing too is that I think the other really strong kind of recollection for me was that very early on you realise that your kids come out with their own personalities.
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是，我觉得另一个非常深刻的记忆是，很早的时候你就意识到你的孩子生来就有他们自己的性格。

sentences.en: And because I too had done a bit of psychology in my time, I think there's that whole nature versus nurture sort of thing that goes through.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我以前也学过一点心理学，我觉得这就是贯穿其中的先天与后天之争。

sentences.en: And I think you start off thinking, you know, you're going to be this amazing parent and it's all going to be nurture.
sentences.zh: 我想你一开始会觉得，你知道的，你要成为一个了不起的父母，这一切全靠后天培养。

sentences.en: But, you know, probably because you were our first, it was a pretty overwhelming kind of sense of, oh, this little person has come out, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，可能因为你是我们的第一个孩子，那种感觉相当震撼，就是“噢，这个小人儿就这么诞生了，

sentences.en: with their own sense of who they are, their own personality.
sentences.zh: 带着他们自己对我是谁的认知，他们自己的个性。”

sentences.en: Um, and then what were you like as a kid?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那小时候的你是什么样的？

sentences.en: I've, you know, you were strong-minded.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，你很有主见。

sentences.en: Um, that hasn't changed much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这点没怎么变。

sentences.en: No, it hasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，确实没变。

sentences.en: But you were, you really, you had strong views even as a, as a youngster, um, but you were happy.
sentences.zh: 但你真的，你甚至在很小的时候就有强烈的观点，嗯，但你很开心。

sentences.en: And as a, the first child for us, the biggest thing was you were a sleeper.
sentences.zh: 而且作为我们的第一个孩子，最棒的一点就是你特别能睡。

sentences.en: And my golly gosh, we love that.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们太喜欢这样了。

sentences.en: That's so cute.
sentences.zh: 太可爱了。

sentences.en: I love that you said I came out and I was quiet for the first week.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你说我一出来第一个星期都很安静。

sentences.en: And the irony being now I literally talk on the internet for my job, which is so funny.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，现在我工作就是 literalmente（字面意思：在互联网上说话），这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: And I am a bit of a yapper, obviously.
sentences.zh: 而且我显然挺能侃的。

sentences.en: I love a yarn.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢聊天。

sentences.en: I love a yarn.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢聊天。

sentences.en: You were just a quiet little mule when you were just a wee little baby.
sentences.zh: 你刚出生当小婴儿的时候，就是一个安静的小不点。

sentences.en: And I was your favourite, obviously, for the first five years at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我显然是至少前五年里你最喜欢的（孩子）。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you, as, as Bart and I say, you're our favourite oldest daughter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，正如巴特（Bart）和我所说，你是我俩最喜欢的长女。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's so diplomatic.
sentences.zh: 对，太外交辞令了。

sentences.en: I still think that you all have a favourite.
sentences.zh: 我还是觉得你们每个人都有一个最喜欢的。

sentences.en: You just can't say.
sentences.zh: 你们只是不能说出口。

sentences.en: And I think that I'm yours.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我就是那个。

sentences.en: That's hopefully my younger sisters, hopefully Ellie and Hannah aren't listening.
sentences.zh: 希望我的妹妹们，希望埃莉（Ellie）和汉娜（Hannah）没有在听。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I'm going to assume they are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，我猜她们肯定在听。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure they are.
sentences.zh: 对，我确信她们在听。

sentences.en: So this is the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这里。

sentences.en: I feel like, how old were you when you had me?
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你生我的时候多大来着？

sentences.en: You were 32, right?
sentences.zh: 你当时32岁，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So you were like, well, well into your 30s, but you were like my age, like nine years older than I am now.
sentences.zh: 所以你就像是，已经步入30多岁了，但你当时就像我这个年纪，比现在的我大九岁。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's like insane to me to think that I would be ready to have a child in nine years, like, let alone in like 15.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直太疯狂了，想到我会在九年内准备好要一个孩子，更不用说在15年内了。

sentences.en: What was like the biggest lesson you learnt having children?
sentences.zh: 生孩子给你上的最大一课是什么？

sentences.en: Did you actually always want children, even when you were younger?
sentences.zh: 你其实一直都想要孩子吗，哪怕在你更年轻的时候？

sentences.en: Yeah, I always wanted kids, even when I was younger.
sentences.zh: 对，我一直都想要孩子，哪怕在我更年轻的时候。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting because like 33 is, you know, it's not young to be having kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这很有趣，因为33岁左右吧，生孩子其实不算年轻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In the spirit of total frankness, you know this, took us a while to get pregnant with you.
sentences.zh: 坦白来说，你知道的，我们花了挺长时间才怀上你。

sentences.en: I don't need the internet to know that.
sentences.zh: 我不需要上网查就知道这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, but it's, you know, and it's just, it is one of those things that, yeah, we, you know,
sentences.zh: 对，嗯，但是，你知道的，而且这，这确实是那种，对，我们，你知道的，

sentences.en: we were keen to have kids, you know, life, you find your partners at whatever age, other things kind of happen.
sentences.zh: 我们很渴望要孩子，你知道的，生活嘛，你在任何年龄都会遇到伴侣，其他事情也会发生。

sentences.en: And, you know, you, I think one of the, one of the things that I was thinking about in terms of this conversation was how people think about when to have kids.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你，我觉得我在考虑这次对话时想到的其中一件事，就是人们是如何看待什么时候要孩子的。

sentences.en: And, you know, for me, it was when I met your dad and, you know, we went overseas and did some things and then came home to Australia and we were keen to start a family.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，对我来说，那是在我遇到你爸爸的时候，你知道的，我们去了海外做了一些事情，然后回到澳大利亚，我们很渴望开始组建家庭。

sentences.en: And, you know, we feel blessed to have three kids, but it's not always a straight line.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们很庆幸能有三个孩子，但这并不总是一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: I definitely felt very ready to be having kids, but it comes with a lot of, you know, a lot
sentences.zh: 我当时确实觉得非常准备好要孩子了，但这也伴随着很多，你知道的，很多

sentences.en: of ups and downs too, and things that you don't know what happens through pregnancies and whatever.
sentences.zh: 起起落落，还有那些你不知道在怀孕期间和其他事情上会发生的事情。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, we, you know, was I ready?
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我们，你知道的，我准备好了吗？

sentences.en: I was, but then in some ways, I guess you're never ready because you never know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我是准备好了，但在某些方面，我想你永远也无法真正准备好，因为你永远不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And that's part of the, the, the challenge is the uncertainty of it all.
sentences.zh: 这也是其中的一部分，这，这种挑战就是这一切的不确定性。

sentences.en: Was it harder when we were younger or is it harder now?
sentences.zh: 是我们小的时候更难带，还是现在更难？

sentences.en: Now that we're, cause we're a lot of us, well, I've, I flew the nest pretty young.
sentences.zh: 既然我们现在，因为我们很多人，好吧，我，我挺年轻就离家独立了。

sentences.en: I left home when I was like 17, but Ellie and Hannah are like getting to the point where they're about to leave.
sentences.zh: 我大概17岁就离开家了，但埃莉（Ellie）和汉娜（Hannah）现在快要到了离开的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Has it been that, has that been difficult being like, oh, am I no longer having that role that you've had for 24 years?
sentences.zh: 那种感觉会不会很难，就是那种，哦，我不再拥有你过去24年里扮演的那种角色了？

sentences.en: I think it's, it's one of the other things you do learn when you have kids.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这，这也是你养育孩子时学到的另一件事。

sentences.en: And maybe I think about this because, you know, you know, I was a working mum for, um, big chunks of, um, you know, your younger life and, and your sisters as well.
sentences.zh: 也许我想起这个是因为，你知道的，你知道的，我在，嗯，你和姐姐们小时候的很大一段人生里，我都是个职业妈妈。

sentences.en: Uh, and particularly, you know, when, when you were in primary school.
sentences.zh: 呃，特别是，你知道的，当，当你在上小学的时候。

sentences.en: And I think there's a sense that when kids are really young, they really need their parents and they do for certain things.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一种观念是，当孩子还很小的时候，他们非常需要父母，而且在某些事情上确实如此。

sentences.en: But, you know, I found when, when you were in high school and your, your sisters, as they've gotten
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我发现当，当你上高中以及你的，你的姐姐们，随着她们长大

sentences.en: older, that, that you continue to need your parents, but in different ways and for different things.
sentences.zh: 以后，你会发现你们依然需要父母，但方式不同，需要的事情也不同。

sentences.en: And, and that sense changes.
sentences.zh: 而且，这种感觉也在改变。

sentences.en: But I, I kind of thought that, you know, there was times when you guys were in high school, for instance, where you needed, um, your parents
sentences.zh: 但我，我曾经以为，你知道的，比如你们在读高中的时候，有些时候你们对

sentences.en: around just as much as you did when we were in primary school.
sentences.zh: 父母的需求并不比我们在小学时少。

sentences.en: And so I think that's maybe one of the, I don't know if myths is the right word, but there's so much focus on, you know, being there for kids when they're younger.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这也许是其中一个，我不知道“神话”是不是合适的词，但人们太专注于，你知道的，在孩子小的时候陪伴在他们身边。

sentences.en: And actually, I think the pressure is there all the way through and just being clear about that and recognising you have to try to find
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我认为这种压力是一直存在的，只要弄清楚这一点，并认识到你必须努力寻找

sentences.en: a way to, to be there for your kids, no matter what else is going on.
sentences.zh: 一种方法，无论发生什么情况，都要陪伴在孩子身边。

sentences.en: It's just one of the, you know, one of the challenges, but also one of the great, um, joys of being a parent
sentences.zh: 这只是其中的一个，你知道的，作为父母的挑战之一，但也是巨大的

sentences.en: when, when you feel like you've, you are doing that and hopefully your kids think, think you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 乐趣之一，当你觉得自己正在这样做，并且希望你的孩子们也认为你在这样做的时候。

sentences.en: Well, it's so interesting because I feel like for a lot of one, like my teenagers, I didn't really need you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太有趣了，因为我觉得对于很多，比如我青少年时期，我其实并不需要你们。

sentences.en: Well, at least I thought I didn't need you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少我以为我不需要你们。

sentences.en: And then as soon as I went to university and then actually like probably the second year of university, like the first year I really was like, I don't need my parents.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦我上了大学，接着实际上可能是在大学第二年，就像第一年的时候我真的觉得，我不需要我的父母。

sentences.en: Like I am a big girl.
sentences.zh: 就像我是一个大姑娘了。

sentences.en: I am an adult now.
sentences.zh: 我现在是个成年人了。

sentences.en: I live independently.
sentences.zh: 我独立生活。

sentences.en: And then it was like, oh, you get older and it's like the reversal and you're like, oh my gosh, I really need my mom.
sentences.zh: 然后就像是，哦，你长大了，这就成了一种反转，你会觉得，哦天哪，我真的很需要我妈妈。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, I really like, it's kind of coming back to the neSt. Like it's such a big thing in your twenties
sentences.zh: 然后我就觉得，哦，我真的很，这有点像是回巢。就像在二十多岁的时候，这是一件大事

sentences.en: that you, you fly the nest and you go off and you do your own thing.
sentences.zh: 你离家独立，出去过你自己的生活。

sentences.en: But then I think that the further along in that journey, the more you're like, actually, I want to come home and like, and I want to see my parents and I want to call my parents.
sentences.zh: 但随后我觉得，在这段旅程中走得越远，你就会越觉得，实际上，我想回家，而且，我想见我的父母，我想给我的父母打电话。

sentences.en: And I remember it was like my first like big heartbreak when I was at uni that I was like suddenly so much
sentences.zh: 我记得我在大学里经历第一次严重的心碎时，我突然变得

sentences.en: more reliant on you guys in a way that I didn't feel like I had been since I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 比我感觉自己还是个孩子以来更加依赖你们了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you all, you know, I've seen it in your sisters as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得你们所有人，你知道的，我也从你姐姐们身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Of course you go through phases of where you really, independence is really important to you and it's, it's the actual independence.
sentences.zh: 当然，你会经历这样一些阶段，在这些阶段里，独立对你来说非常重要，而且是真正的独立。

sentences.en: And I think it's the perception of independence as well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也是对独立的感知问题。

sentences.en: Um, but I think, you know, from my perspective, just being around sometimes is important then.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为，你知道的，从我的角度来看，有时候陪伴在身边在当时是很重要的。

sentences.en: So, you know, because I think it allows you to sort of go off and, um, and live your life, but knowing that if you need it, it's there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，因为我认为这能让你去，嗯，过你自己的生活，但心里知道如果需要的话，支持就在那里。

sentences.en: And even if you don't necessarily acknowledge it, I think there's a sense that, you know, you, your parents can provide a bit of a foundation and,
sentences.zh: 即使你未必承认，我也觉得有一种感觉，你知道的，你的父母可以为你提供一些基础，并且，

sentences.en: you know, if you do need to come back or need support, we're there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你真的需要回来或者需要支持，我们都在。

sentences.en: But it's, you know, the flip side is it's, it's fantastic as a parent to see your kids going off and doing that.
sentences.zh: 但，你知道的，另一面是，作为父母，看到孩子们展翅高飞去过那种生活，感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: Uh, and then, yeah, hopefully at different stages, the perception or whatever of that independence becomes less important.
sentences.zh: 呃，然后，对，希望在不同的阶段，对那种独立的感知或其他什么会变得不那么重要。

sentences.en: And you, and that's the whole thing about it.
sentences.zh: 而你，这就是整件事情的意义所在。

sentences.en: Your relationship kind of ebbs and flows and evolves.
sentences.zh: 你们的关系会有起有伏，不断演变。

sentences.en: And it's, yeah, it's a, it's a nice thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，对，这是一件美好的事情。

sentences.en: What's been the hardest part about being a mother?
sentences.zh: 做母亲最艰难的部分是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, it's a good question.
sentences.zh: 对，这，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I think in all honesty, um, it's the sort of vulnerability and the uncertainty of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得说实话，嗯，那种脆弱感和不确定性就是最艰难的。

sentences.en: Um, like you just, you know, with a partner, there's an element of it, but when you, you know, when you have kids and you just love them
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像你只是，你知道的，和伴侣在一起时会有这种成分，但当你，你知道的，当你有了孩子，你只是非常爱他们

sentences.en: so much and care for them so much, it's that, you know, watching them go out into the world and
sentences.zh: 非常关心他们，那种，你知道的，看着他们走向世界，

sentences.en: the equal measure of wanting them to be independent and, and, you know, excited and exploring the world and doing everything that you did.
sentences.zh: 一方面希望他们独立，而且，你知道的，感到兴奋、探索世界并做你做过的一切。

sentences.en: But, uh, you know, also sort of probably having a greater understanding of all the things that can go wrong.
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，你知道的，可能也更深刻地理解了所有可能出错的事情。

sentences.en: And it's just that balance of just, you know, there's always just that little bit of fear.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种平衡，你知道的，总会有那么一点点恐惧。

sentences.en: You never want harm or sadness or anything to come to your kids, but that's not the way they can live their lives.
sentences.zh: 你永远不希望伤害、悲伤或任何不好的事降临到你的孩子身上，但这并不是他们生活的方式。

sentences.en: So it's just that uncertainty and it's, you know, it brings great excitement and emotion and joy.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是那种不确定性，而且，你知道的，它带来了巨大的兴奋、情感和快乐。

sentences.en: Uh, but every now and then, you know, you're, you're white knuckling it a bit.
sentences.zh: 呃，但每隔一段时间，你知道的，你还是会有点提心吊胆。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: It's so interesting because I even feel that way towards Hannah and Ellie, like my sisters, where Ellie is going to uni and I think about what
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了，因为我对汉娜和埃莉（我的姐姐们）甚至也有这种感觉，比如埃莉要去上大学了，我想起了

sentences.en: my first two years of uni are like, and I want her to have those experiences, but I also know like how chaotic and sometimes awful they were.
sentences.zh: 我大一和大二时的经历，我希望她能有那些经历，但我也知道那些经历是多么混乱，有时甚至是糟糕的。

sentences.en: And I'm like, maybe I'll just protect you from them.
sentences.zh: 我想着，也许我该保护她免受这些伤害。

sentences.en: Like, maybe you could just be a little girl, little, a little baby for a little bit longer and like, not have those, that independence.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许你可以再当一会儿小女孩，小，一个小宝宝，不要那么快拥有那种独立性。

sentences.en: And I'm like, I feel that towards my sister.
sentences.zh: 然后我就觉得，我对我的妹妹也有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I can't imagine what that would feel like as a mother being like, I gave birth to this child who was now like doing like off in the world.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法想象，作为一个母亲会是什么感觉——生下了这个现在已经，你知道的，去外面闯荡的孩子。

sentences.en: And I like, don't know what they're, where they are.
sentences.zh: 而我，不知道他们在哪里。

sentences.en: I don't know what they're doing at all times.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道他们每时每刻在做什么。

sentences.en: What was like an experience where you said you were like white knuckling it?
sentences.zh: 有什么经历能让你说你当时是在“提心吊胆”吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it's, you know, there's things, well, I don't know, you go overseas.
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道的，有些事情，嗯，我不知道，你去海外的时候。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, are you thinking about that time I was in Amsterdam and I called you and was like,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，你在想那次我在阿姆斯特丹给你打电话说

sentences.en: I'm dying?
sentences.zh: 快要死了的事情吗？

sentences.en: Possibly.
sentences.zh: 有可能。

sentences.en: And I wasn't even like on anything.
sentences.zh: 而且我当时甚至什么都没碰。

sentences.en: I wasn't, I know the connotations of like being in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 我没有，我知道在阿姆斯特丹那种地方意味着什么。

sentences.en: I was just like really tired.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是真的很累。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm dying.
sentences.zh: 然后我就说，我要死了。

sentences.en: I've decided like my anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我决定了，我的焦虑症发作了。

sentences.en: And I called you guys like 3am.
sentences.zh: 然后我在凌晨3点左右给你们打电话。

sentences.en: Well, and it was, it was the, um, you know, it was that like, maybe white knuckling is the, the, the wrong way to describe it, but there is a
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时，当时，嗯，你知道的，就像是，也许“提心吊胆”是，是，用来形容这个词不太对，但确实有

sentences.en: certain sense that when your phone rings in the middle of the night, you know, once you've had kids
sentences.zh: 一种感觉，就是当你的电话在半夜响起时，你知道的，一旦你有了孩子

sentences.en: that, that has a certain, like you leap to, you can leap to the wrong conclusion.
sentences.zh: 那就会有一种特定的感觉，比如你会立刻，你会往坏处想。

sentences.en: And so you, your heart starts racing.
sentences.zh: 所以你的心跳开始加速。

sentences.en: Um, you calm yourself down, but then, you know, there was an element of, gee, it would have been nice if you'd phone the next day to remind us that you were okay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你让自己平静下来，但是，你知道的，这里面有一种情绪，天哪，你要是第二天打个电话提醒我们你没事就好了。

sentences.en: No, no, that's not how it works.
sentences.zh: 不，不，事情可不是这样的。

sentences.en: I was too, so I was 18 and selfish.
sentences.zh: 我当时才18岁，还很自私。

sentences.en: I wasn't going to let you guys know I was okay.
sentences.zh: 我才不会让你们知道我没事呢。

sentences.en: But the other, but the other thing too, is just, um, the emotional sort of stuff and the emotional hurt.
sentences.zh: 但另一个，但另一件事是，嗯，情感上的种种以及情感上的伤害。

sentences.en: And so that's why, you know, white knuckling is not the right term, but you do expose yourself to feeling it in, you know, you've experienced it yourself,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么，你知道的，“提心吊胆”虽然不是准确的词，但你确实让自己去感受它，你知道的，你自己也经历过，

sentences.en: but then to watch other people who you care about go through some of that stuff, which is just,
sentences.zh: 但接着去看着其他你在乎的人经历其中的一些事情，这就，

sentences.en: it's just life, but you know, it's, it's not, it's not easy to see other people go through that and to be sad or, um, to be, you know, to be hurt.
sentences.zh: 这只是生活，但你知道的，看着别人经历这些并感到难过，或者，嗯，受到伤害，真的不容易。

sentences.en: And in some ways, really the emotional stuff is harder than, you know, going to get the stitches, um, or whatever else.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，情感上的事情其实比，你知道的，去缝针，嗯，或者其他什么还要难受。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've had conversations about this, that, you know, we've, we try to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们讨论过这个，你知道的，我们尽量去做正确的事。

sentences.en: We try to, to raise each of you as independent, um, people who could make their own decisions and who were resilient to those challenges.
sentences.zh: 我们试图，把你们每个人培养成独立的，嗯，能够自己做决定并且能够从容应对这些挑战的人。

sentences.en: And sometimes it meant, you know, letting you find your way a bit.
sentences.zh: 有时候这意味着，你知道的，让你们自己去摸索一段时间。

sentences.en: And, and I'm sure that felt hard and it's, it was hard to watch, but, um, and experience as well,
sentences.zh: 而且，我确信那感觉很难，看着很难，但，嗯，经历起来也很难，

sentences.en: but you've got to, you know, it's always trying to walk that line of doing things that, that,
sentences.zh: 但你必须，你知道的，这总是在努力把握好分寸，去做那些，

sentences.en: you know, trying to be the parent that sets you up for success in your future, um, which
sentences.zh: 你知道的，努力做一个为你未来的成功打下基础的父母，嗯，这

sentences.en: sometimes, you know, comes across as, you know, not necessarily being the kindest or most protective parent at different stages when you're younger.
sentences.zh: 有时，你知道的，在不同的阶段，当你还小的时候，看起来可能并不一定是最善良或最保护你的父母。

sentences.en: I know exactly what you're referring to.
sentences.zh: 我完全知道你在指什么。

sentences.en: And I remember being in primary school and all of the people, all of my friends had these like helicopter parents who had a drop of a hat would be there to fix things for them.
sentences.zh: 我记得我上小学时，所有的人，我所有的朋友都有那种“直升机父母”，一有风吹草动就会赶来帮他们解决问题。

sentences.en: And you guys were not those parents.
sentences.zh: 而你们不是那种父母。

sentences.en: You were like, Oh, you're having problems at school.
sentences.zh: 你们会说，哦，你在学校遇到麻烦了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Go and talk to your teacher.
sentences.zh: 去找你的老师谈谈。

sentences.en: Deal with it.
sentences.zh: 自己处理。

sentences.en: Like not that callous.
sentences.zh: 倒也不是那么冷酷无情。

sentences.en: You weren't like, deal with it.
sentences.zh: 你们不会说，自己看着办。

sentences.en: Like get out of our face.
sentences.zh: 就像别在我们面前烦我们。

sentences.en: We don't want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 我们不想听你诉苦。

sentences.en: But it was like that thing where I did have a point where I was like, gosh, I wish that my mom was just like a bit more angry on like on my behalf.
sentences.zh: 但确实有那么一段时间，我心想，天哪，我真希望我妈妈能为我多生点气。

sentences.en: And I'm sure grateful for the fact that you made me be a problem solver and independent because it's, I think, a big part of my personality.

sentences.en: It tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: 它追踪我的身体负荷、恢复情况、压力，以及最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有这些数据和模式，以便我能做出更好的决定，这包括知道什么时候该轻松一点，什么时候该全力以赴。

sentences.en: New members can try whoop with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅会员之前，可以先通过 Whoop 30 天免费试用来体验。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of whoop.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com 斜杠 psychology 获取你的 Whoop 免费体验月。

sentences.en: This is the loudest show of the summer.
sentences.zh: 这是今年夏天最吵闹的节目。

sentences.en: This January, the United Cup comes to town and it will not be quiet.
sentences.zh: 今年一月，联合杯（United Cup）即将开赛，现场注定不会安静。

sentences.en: There will be roaring.
sentences.zh: 这里将有震耳欲聋的呐喊。

sentences.en: There will be chanting.
sentences.zh: 这里将有此起彼伏的助威。

sentences.en: There will be entire nations losing their voices at once.
sentences.zh: 这里将有成千上万的人同时呐喊到嘶哑。

sentences.en: So to everyone within earshot, here's an invitation.
sentences.zh: 所以对于所有在场的人，在此发出邀请。

sentences.en: If you can't beat the noise, come and bring it.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法战胜这喧嚣，那就加入并制造它。
